change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admin check uses `&&`, so only owners pass
findings.body: `isTeamAdmin` already matches role ADMIN or OWNER (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:270), and `isTeamOwner` matches only OWNER (:292). Joining them with `&&` means a team ADMIN who isn't the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN. Calling `isTeamAdmin` alone is enough. Hosts of collective bookings are also left out: `bookingsProcedure` allows them (util.ts:34-43), but this check doesn't.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased (line 71), but `guest` is compared as typed. Entering `Foo@x.com` gets past a blacklisted `foo@x.com`. The check against existing attendees is also an exact `===` match (line 76), so `Bob@x.com` is added as a second row for attendee `bob@x.com`. Lowercase both sides of each comparison.

findings.title: Server accepts unbounded, duplicate guest lists
findings.body: Only the dialog checks that emails are unique (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29). The API schema has no dedupe and no maximum length. A request with `[a@x.com, a@x.com]` creates two attendee rows through `createMany` (handler.ts:100-104), and each row gets an email. The handler also lets any attendee call it (handler.ts:52-54). So anyone who has booked can send any number of addresses and have cal.com email all of them. Dedupe the list, lowercase it, and set a `.max()` on the array.

findings.title: Emails are sent for the raw `guests` list, not `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses the unfiltered input. A guest who was already an attendee, and so was filtered out at line 76, is still in `newGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts:541-542) that attendee gets a full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, a new-booking confirmation, instead of the add-guests notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Calendar update runs with the caller's credentials, and a failure after the DB write is unrecoverable
findings.body: `EventManager` is built from `ctx.user`'s credentials, the same way editLocation does it (editLocation.handler.ts:97-105). But editLocation only lets organizers and collective hosts in (util.ts:30-44). Here an attendee or a team admin can be the caller, and their credentials don't own the booking's calendar references. So the organizer's calendar event probably won't get the new attendees. Also, `updateCalendarAttendees` (line 165) isn't wrapped in try/catch and runs after the attendees are already written (lines 92-106). If it throws, the user sees an error and no emails go out. A retry then filters every guest out as a duplicate and returns `emails_must_be_unique_valid`. Use the organizer's credentials (`booking.user.credentials` is already included), and catch or log calendar failures the way editLocation does (lines 109-114).

findings.title: Validation error never clears
findings.body: `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is only reset by the Cancel button (line 91). The error stays after the user fixes the emails. It also survives a successful submit (onSuccess, lines 36-41, doesn't reset it) and closing the dialog with Escape or the overlay (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, line 61). The next time the dialog opens, it shows "Emails must be unique and valid" before the user has typed anything. Reset the flag on success, on any close, and on a valid submit.

findings.title: Error fallback can never be used
findings.body: `message` is a template string, so it's never empty, and `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` always uses `message`. When `err.data` is missing, the toast reads "undefined: …". Server messages that aren't translation keys come through raw.

findings.title: New guests are stored with an empty name
findings.body: Each guest is created with `name: ""`. The emails then go to `" <email>"` (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:19, and the same in the scheduled email), and greetings and attendee lists show a blank name. Falling back to the email's local part would read better.

contracts.before_after: editLocation is gated by bookingsProcedure (organizer or collective host) and writes to the DB only after the calendar update succeeds. addGuests runs its own looser check (attendees, owners only) and writes to the DB before the calendar update, which isn't wrapped in try/catch.
contracts.visible_effect: On success, a toast and invalidated bookings queries refresh the list (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-41).
contracts.failure_mode: If updateCalendarAttendees throws, attendees are already stored, no emails go out, and a retry returns emails_must_be_unique_valid.

contracts.action: Open Add guests dialog from booking actions
contracts.equivalent_path: Edit location dialog in the same editBookingActions list
contracts.before_after: Shown only for upcoming bookings that aren't cancelled, like the other edit actions. Dialog state isn't reset when it's closed by Escape or the overlay.
contracts.visible_effect: Leftover email values and the validation error stay visible when the dialog is reopened.
contracts.failure_mode: The validation error flag stays set.

summary: The add-guests feature works on the happy path, but the handler has several defects. The admin check uses `&&`, so only team owners pass. The blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive. The server schema doesn't dedupe or cap the guest list, and any attendee can call the endpoint. Emails go out for the unfiltered `guests` list. The calendar update uses the caller's credentials, and it runs after the DB write with no error handling. In the dialog, the validation error is never cleared.
